caption_hook: 🐢 Jonathan the giant tortoise is at least 194, and scientists just found clues to his long life in his DNA + 3 more wins you missed 👇
question: Describe Jonathan in one emoji 👇
share_line: Send this to the oldest friend you have
first_comment: Bonus: his vet collected DNA with a cheek swab, because officials on Saint Helena didn't allow a blood draw from such an elderly, beloved tortoise. What would you ask Jonathan? 🐢

stories.headline: A 194-year-old tortoise's DNA hints at his long-life secret
stories.summary: Scientists read the genome of Jonathan, the oldest known land animal. In 272 of his genes, the chemical on/off switches stayed as orderly as a young tortoise's. He also has unique variants in 287 genes.
stories.why: Learning how Jonathan stays healthy could inform research on human ageing.

stories.headline: A 30-minute hot bath lowered blood pressure more than cycling
stories.summary: In a small study of 25 adults aged 45 to 70, a 30-minute soak at 40°C widened blood vessels and lowered blood pressure more than 30 minutes of moderate cycling.
stories.why: It may help people who can't easily exercise. It's no substitute for exercise, though.

stories.stat_label: of solar panels imported in 3 years
stories.headline: Pakistan brought in about 41 GW of solar panels in 3 years
stories.summary: Pakistan imported about 7.6 GW of solar panels in 2023, 16.4 GW in 2024 and 16.9 GW in 2025. Most were bought by households, farms, shops and factories, not the government.
stories.why: Ordinary people are powering a country's switch to clean energy.

stories.stat_label: lighthouse image found on a signet ring
stories.headline: Divers found a ring engraved with the Lighthouse of Alexandria
stories.summary: Underwater archaeologists found a bronze signet ring showing the lighthouse at the sunken palace of Antirhodos. It is the first known engraving of the Wonder on a signet ring.
stories.why: It's a rare new glimpse of a Wonder that crumbled centuries ago.

fun_fact: The Lighthouse of Alexandria is thought to have stood more than 100 metres tall.
